title: friends before the fire
hookLine: two exiles walk around a fire and become friends
carry: sakhya, friendship sworn before the fire

cards: Two exiles meet on a mountaintop. One is a prince who lost his kingdom and then his wife. The other is a monkey prince who lost his kingdom and his wife to his own brother.
They've never seen each other before today. Both have been betrayed, or think they have. How do you start a friendship between two people with every reason to be careful?
Valmiki's answer involves fire, and it's Hanuman who sets it up.

teach.b: Hanuman arranges it. He brings wood, kindles a fire between them, and honors it with flowers. Rama and Sugriva walk around the fire together, keeping it to their right, the way a bride and groom do at a Hindu wedding.
Then they say to each other, in effect: from now on, your joy is my joy, and your sorrow is my sorrow. Why fire?
In Hindu ritual, Agni, the fire, carries offerings to the gods and witnesses vows.

That's the reason the fire sits at the center of a Hindu wedding: the couple's promises are made in front of a witness that can't be argued with. Rama and Sugriva use the same witness for a friendship.
Sugriva breaks off a flowering branch and spreads it on the ground, and he and Rama sit on it together. Hanuman breaks off another for Lakshmana. Two exiles side by side: neither patron nor beggar.
Then, what each one needs. Sugriva's brother Vali has taken his kingdom and his wife. Rama promises to deal with Vali.
Sugriva promises to help find Sita.
It's a deal, yes, but the poem frames it as friendship first. The word is sakhya, the bond of a sakha, a friend.
Later the Bhagavata Purana counts sakhya among the ways of loving God: God as a friend, the way Arjuna loves Krishna. So in this tradition, friendship isn't small. Sworn honestly, it can be holy.

how: In a Hindu wedding the couple walks around the sacred fire with Agni called on as witness (the number of rounds and steps varies by custom); Rama and Sugriva's circling of the fire uses that same gesture for friendship.

o: friendship, the bond between two friends
a fire ritual that seals a wedding vow
a royal treaty between two kingdoms at war

p: Rama and Sugriva sit on it together

s: Rama and Sugriva seal their friendship with a handshake
they walk around a fire together, as at a wedding.
the pact is framed as friendship, not only a deal
your joy is mine, your sorrow is mine.
Rama sits above Sugriva as his patron
they sit side by side on the same branch.

games.q: at a Hindu wedding, a friend asks why the couple walks around a fire. by Rama and Sugriva's story, what fits?
o: Agni, the fire, is the witness: the vows are made in front of it.
the fire keeps the couple warm through a long ceremony.
the fire is just decoration for the photos.
games.why: Hanuman kindled a fire, and Rama and Sugriva circled it, making Agni the witness of their friendship, as a couple does at a wedding.

practice: If you have a diya or a candle, light it; if not, picture a small flame in front of you. Bring one friend to mind. Breathe in and remember a time their sorrow felt like yours; breathe out and remember a time their joy did too.
If you pray, hold them before the flame, the way Rama and Sugriva held their promise before Agni.

wordCard.voice: Sakhya, the bond of a sakha, a friend: sworn today around a fire between Rama and Sugriva, your joy is mine and your sorrow is mine.

orig.note: Sanskrit sakhya: friendship, the bond of a sakha (friend). later counted among the forms of devotion.

carryVoice: Your line: sakhya, friendship sworn before the fire. Your joy is my joy, your sorrow is my sorrow. Day five hundred eighty-three, done.
